findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on IO errors (file not found, permission denied, etc.)
findings.failure_mode: Untrusted or missing file path aborts the entire program instead of returning a typed I/O error
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, io::Error>. Propagate fs::read_to_string errors with ? or match, and wrap in a domain-appropriate error type.

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on invalid input (non-numeric, out of range for u16)
findings.failure_mode: A single malformed line aborts the entire token list instead of yielding a per-record parse error
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, RecordError>. Use parts.get(1).ok_or(MissingField) and parse with map_err to produce a typed ParseError per record.

findings.problem: Lossy cast as u16 from u32 silently truncates values outside u16 range (0-65535)
findings.failure_mode: A valid u32 value > 65535 silently wraps to a wrong u16, corrupting data without any error signal
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from(parsed_u32) or parse directly to u16 with parts[1].parse::<u16>(), returning an overflow error instead of truncating.

findings.problem: Unchecked indexing parts[0] without bounds check
findings.failure_mode: If a line has zero fields, parts[0] panics with index-out-of-bounds
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') and handle the None case, or parts.first().ok_or(MissingField) for a safe access.

findings.problem: Unchecked indexing parts[1] without bounds check
findings.failure_mode: If a line has only one comma-separated field, parts[1] panics with index-out-of-bounds
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') expecting exactly two fields, or parts.get(1).ok_or(MissingValueField).

findings.problem: println!() side effect inside the map iterator of a data-parsing function
findings.failure_mode: Logging inside the pure data pipeline couples output to data processing, makes the function non-deterministic (stdout ordering), and prevents testing the parsing logic without capturing stderr/stdout
findings.fix: Remove println! from the parser. If logging is needed, push log events as part of the return type or handle logging in the shell layer after parsing completes.

findings.problem: load_tokens mixes I/O (fs::read_to_string) with parsing logic in a single function with no error boundary
findings.failure_mode: The pure parsing logic cannot be unit-tested in isolation from file system operations, and all failure modes (IO, parsing, indexing) are conflated into a panicking Vec return
findings.fix: Split into a pure parse_records(Iterator<&str>) -> Result<Vec<Record>, RecordError> in the core, and a shell function load_tokens(path) -> Result<Vec<Record>, AppError> that handles I/O and calls the core.

findings.problem: split(',') + collect() into Vec<String> allocates all parts unnecessarily when only the first two fields are needed
findings.failure_mode: Each line allocates a Vec of Strings even for a 2-field record. For large files this is wasteful memory pressure and GC/allocator load
findings.fix: Use line.split_once(',') to get the first two fields without collecting all parts, then trim each individually.

findings.problem: parts[0].clone() clones an already-owned String unnecessarily
findings.failure_mode: Extra allocation per record. The String is already owned in the Vec and can be moved directly.
findings.fix: Move the String directly from the iterator (use split_once and move the &str results into String::from, or use into() without collect).

residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. The crate contains multiple panic-on-unknown-input paths (unwrap on IO, unwrap on parse, unchecked indexing) and a lossy cast. All are recoverable with Result types, split_once, get/first, and try_from.
